annotation.title_clean: D1.2 Ethics Framework: Managing active and healthy aging with use of caring service robots
annotation.title_en: D1.2 Ethics Framework: Managing active and healthy aging with use of caring service robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Beyan, T.; Felzmann, H.; Ryan, M.; Lang, N.; Beyan, O.
annotation.venue: MARIO Project (H2020 grant 643808) deliverable, European Commission
annotation.summary_en: An EU Horizon 2020 MARIO project deliverable by NUI Galway. It sets out a multi-layered ethics framework for care robots that support older people with dementia. Drawing on a literature review and lessons from earlier projects, it examines care roles, quality of care, robot functions and design features, with a focus on privacy, dignity and autonomy. It then applies the framework to MARIO use cases.
key_provisions_or_claims: Care robots are double-edged: they can either infringe or improve ethical values in elder care
Framework analyses four layers: integration into care, quality of care, robotic functionalities, core capabilities/design features
Humanoid appearance should be used only as far as needed for reasonable design goals, given deception and uncanny-valley concerns
Data protection and privacy must be built into the design process (value sensitive design)
Dementia-specific ethical issues, such as informed consent and capacity, need particular attention
